metadata.name: [GCP BigQuery OTel] Interactive queries queueing
metadata.description: Alerts when interactive-priority query jobs are pending (queued) in at least 10 one-minute samples in the last 30 minutes for a project and location. Batch-priority queueing is excluded; see the batch backlog rule. One alert per project and location.

query.base:
TS metrics-gcp.bigquery.otel-*
// Interactive-priority query jobs waiting in PENDING state (batch priority is designed to wait; see the backlog rule)
| WHERE resource.attributes.gcp.resource_type == "bigquery_project"
  AND attributes.state == "pending"
  AND attributes.job_type == "query"
  AND attributes.priority == "interactive"
// Stage 1: one value per minute per logical series (MAX collapses fragmented TSIDs of the same series)
| STATS pending = MAX(MAX_OVER_TIME(`metrics.bigquery.googleapis.com/job/num_in_flight`))
    BY @timestamp = TBUCKET(1 minute), resource.attributes.project_id, resource.attributes.location
| WHERE pending IS NOT NULL
// Customise: a minute counts as queued when >= 1 interactive query is pending
| STATS queued_minutes = COUNT(*) WHERE pending >= 1,
        reported_minutes = COUNT(*),
        peak_pending_jobs = MAX(pending),
        avg_pending_jobs = ROUND(AVG(pending), 1)
    BY resource.attributes.project_id, resource.attributes.location

data.content:
## BigQuery interactive queries queueing

Interactive-priority queries are waiting in `PENDING` state. Users and BI tools wait longer for results. This is the closest latency signal available, because the query execution time distribution is not collected.

### Condition
- Per minute: `job/num_in_flight` for `state == "pending"`, `job_type == "query"`, and `priority == "interactive"` (`bigquery_project` resource).
- Alert when >= 1 job is pending in >= 10 one-minute samples within the 30-minute look-back. `job/num_in_flight` publishes up to ~12 minutes late, so about 18 minutes are visible. Unpublished minutes are not counted as either healthy or queued.

### Triage
1. Open the [GCP OTel] BigQuery dashboard and filter to the project and location. Check queue depth by priority, slots allocated, and queries in flight.
2. Capacity model: check the reservation saturation alert or panel for the reservation the project is assigned to.
3. On-demand: check whether the project is near its on-demand slot cap or has hit its interactive query concurrency limit.
4. Look for a burst of new queries, such as a BI dashboard refresh storm or a newly deployed scheduler.

### Remediation
- Add capacity (reservation baseline or autoscale max), reduce concurrency at the source, or move non-urgent work to batch priority.

### Tuning
- `pending >= 1`: minimum queue depth for a minute to count. Increase it for projects where short queueing is normal.
- `queued_minutes >= 10`: persistence. Keep this below the visible minutes (~18 for a 30-minute look-back) or extend the look-back.

### Notes
- Data: `metrics-gcp.bigquery.otel-*` (OTel `googlecloudmonitoring` receiver). Dashboard: [GCP OTel] BigQuery.
- GCP publishes BigQuery metrics with a delay, so the look-back is longer than the condition and the newest minutes are never treated as zero.
- The query returns at most 50 breaching rows; each returned row is one alert. Thresholds are marked `// Customise:` in the query.
